## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double anonymous: "All submissions are sent to at least 2 independent and anonymous reviewers" after editorial-office screening (home-page copy dated 2026-11-05; guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15). The guidelines' pre-submission checklist says to check that no author names appear anywhere in the manuscript, including figures and captions, and gives as a tip the wording "previous research has demonstrated" rather than "our previous research" for one's own work |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Partly: the guidelines describe an Emerald manuscript transfer service in which the editor may recommend a transfer to another participating Emerald journal, and reviewer reports go along if the author accepts. Whether this journal participates was not stated |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not stated |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No source found. The guidelines say the editor may accept, request minor or major revisions, or decline |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source stating that authors may suggest reviewers was found |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No separate journal text: the guidelines carry the publisher's AI paragraph and refer to the publisher's Publishing Ethics page for examples (copy dated 2026-08-15). The Emerald policy applies |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | Partly: the Editor and Publisher reserve the right to decide whether an AI tool's use is permissible (guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 (this pass's own rubric: allowed with mandatory disclosure = 3, lowered by one because generating new material with generative AI is stated as not permitted) |
| **Summary** | Large language models cannot be credited as authors. Authors must describe the content created or modified and cite the name and version of the AI tool. Copywriting any part of a submission with generative AI to generate new material is not permitted; copy-editing the author's own existing text to improve structure, clarity, language and grammar is permitted. Standard spelling and grammar tools are outside the guidance. Retrieved via Wayback copy dated 2026-08-15 |

## Format

> Source: the journal's author-guidelines page (Wayback copy dated 2026-08-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260815101628/https://www.emeraldgrouppublishing.com/journal/jd) and its home page (copy dated 2026-11-05, https://web.archive.org/web/20261105234243/https://www.emerald.com/jd). The two copies differ on some limits; both are given.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Submission types: Article, Review, Short Review (guidelines); the home-page copy also lists Editorial. Categories: research paper, viewpoint, technical paper, conceptual paper, case study, literature review, general review. The aims text adds "Speculation in Documentation" contributions |
| **Word limit** | Guidelines copy (2026-08-15): articles between 4,000 and 10,000 words including structured abstract, references, tables, figures and appendices, 250 words allowed per figure or table. Home-page copy (2026-11-05): Article up to 10,000, Review up to 10,000, Short Review up to 4,500, Editorial up to 3,000, 280 words per figure or table. The aims text: Speculation in Documentation at most 5,000 words |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. Not stated |
| **Abstract limit** | Structured abstract, at most 250 words including keywords and article classification; headings Purpose, Design/methodology/approach, Findings, Originality (required) and three optional ones (guidelines copy 2026-08-15) |
| **Reference limit** | No cap; references count inside the word total (guidelines copy 2026-08-15). Harvard style required (any recognised Harvard style accepted) |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed; host on the publisher's platform or a trusted repository, all submitted before acceptance, not copy-edited; extensive supplementary material may itself be peer reviewed (guidelines copy 2026-08-15) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit; tables go in a separate file, figures in listed formats (.ai, .eps, .jpeg, .bmp, .tif) |
| **Style / submission format** | Word files (LaTeX only with an accompanying PDF); UK or US English only; keywords: up to 12 in the guidelines copy and up to 6 in the home-page copy; ScholarOne submission only, by the authors themselves; author biographies and acknowledgements as separate files; anonymised manuscript |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** A scope condition is stated: the journal publishes "research papers with novel methods or results of wide significance, in all the information-related disciplines", welcomes critical and scholarly reviews, reviews of the evidence base for professional practice and shorter speculative articles, and describes itself as linking research, scholarship and reflective professional practice (aims text, https://web.archive.org/web/20260815101628/https://www.emeraldgrouppublishing.com/journal/jd, copy dated 2026-08-15).
- **What kind of engagement?** Theory, concepts, models, frameworks and philosophies about documents and recorded knowledge (home-page copy dated 2026-11-05, https://web.archive.org/web/20261105234243/https://www.emerald.com/jd); particular welcome for topics where library and information science concepts overlap with cognate disciplines (aims text). The guidelines tell authors to read the aims and scope first because "the editor may decline it without peer review" if the manuscript does not fit.
- **Article type and length**: Article, Review or Short Review; up to 10,000 words including references (see Format), structured abstract of at most 250 words.
- **Special-issue framing seen**: none: the home-page copy of 2026-11-05 says there are no open calls for papers.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: stated: the editorial office may decline or un-submit manuscripts that do not fit submission policies, aims and scope, or whose language or manuscript quality is too low (guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15). No desk-rejection percentage exists.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex: 555 records, 550 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex named in the regex table (AI-Research Notes). Shares use 550 as denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement or a clearly dominant count. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 2 | experiments or user studies 20 (3.6%); surveys or questionnaires 73 (13.3%); "quantitative" 39 (7.1%). The score follows the experiments count; surveys alone would score 3 |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | interviews 153 (27.8%); "qualitative" 134 (24.4%). No editorial statement on qualitative work found |
| Autoethnography | 2 | Ethnography or autoethnography terms 19 (3.5%) (the regex does not separate the two) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 4 | theory or conceptual wording 250 (45.5%), a dominant count; editorial statement: the journal describes a focus on "theories, concepts, models, frameworks and philosophies" (home-page copy dated 2026-11-05, https://web.archive.org/web/20261105234243/https://www.emerald.com/jd). The regex is broad, since "theory" also appears in applied papers |

| Case study (added row) | 3 | 45 (8.2%) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Strict, in writing: for research involving human participants authors must obtain informed consent and, where appropriate, give an ethical statement naming the ethics committee and its location, the approval number and date and the guidelines followed; work without a suitable statement is returned and may be rejected (guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260815101628/https://www.emeraldgrouppublishing.com/journal/jd). Authors must also decide whether ethical approval is needed and say so |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are common: 195 of 532 articles in the window, 36.7% (OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No independent-scholar rule stated. Author affiliation is taken from the submission account and should be where the author was based when the research was conducted (guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15). One advisory-board entry prints a project name (EIFL PLIP) rather than a university department, and one prints no affiliation or country (copy dated 2026-08-15); this says nothing about acceptance odds |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The publisher is a signatory of the Transparency and Openness Promotion guidelines and encourages citing data and code with persistent identifiers; no deposit mandate is stated (guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double anonymous review: no author names anywhere in the manuscript, including figures and captions; acknowledgements and biographies go in separate files; links to repositories can reveal identity (guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15). The preprint rule was not read, so the effect of a public preprint is unknown |
| **AI use** | Disclose created or modified content and name the tool and version; generating new material with generative AI is not permitted (AI Policy) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; no submission fee: the page says money is asked only for gold open access, after acceptance; APC amount not read (Open Access) |
| **Conflicts and permissions** | Conflicts of interest are declared at submission; third-party permissions must be cleared before submission; Crossref Similarity Check may be used (guidelines copy dated 2026-08-15) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 4 (99.1% of records have abstracts); journal-specific policies and guidelines 3 (two Wayback copies of the journal's own pages, dated 2026-08-15 and 2026-11-05, which differ on word limits, keyword limits and metrics); board 3 (copy dated 2026-08-15); publisher-wide policies 2 (pointers only, policy pages unread); experiential layer 0.

**Keyword regex table** (Python `re`, case-insensitive unless noted; applied to title plus reconstructed abstract of each OpenAlex record with an abstract; denominator 550; script run 2026-11-23):

| Name | Regex | Hits |
|------|-------|------|
| surveys or questionnaires | `\b(surveys?\|questionnaires?)\b` | 73 |
| interviews | `\binterview(s\|ed\|ing)?\b` | 153 |
| qualitative | `\bqualitative\b` | 134 |
| quantitative | `\bquantitative\b` | 39 |
| experiments or user studies | `\b(experiments?\|experimental\|user stud(y\|ies)\|randomi[sz]ed)\b` | 20 |
| bibliometric or scientometric | `\b(bibliometric\w*\|scientometric\w*\|citation analysis\|co-citation\|altmetric\w*)\b` | 28 |
| machine learning or language models | `\b(machine learning\|deep learning\|neural network\w*\|large language models?\|LLMs?\|transformers?\|natural language processing)\b` | 32 |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Anonymisation**: review is double anonymous, and the guidelines require that no author names appear anywhere, including figures and captions (Peer Review, Practical Concerns; copy dated 2026-08-15).
- **Ethics statement**: research with human participants needs informed consent and, where appropriate, a written ethical statement; work without them is returned (Practical Concerns).
- **Generative AI**: generating new material with generative AI is stated as not permitted; use must be described and the tool and version named (AI Policy).
- **Length**: the home-page copy gives 10,000 words as the ceiling for Articles and Reviews including references; the guidelines copy sets 4,000 to 10,000 for articles (Format). The two copies disagree on the floor, so check the live page.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher reports 29.5 to 37 days to first decision and 47 to 50 days from acceptance to publication in two page copies (Review Cycle Time); no total-time or first-hand figure exists.
- **Fit screening**: the editorial office may decline manuscripts on fit or language quality before review, and the publisher reports a 26.2% to 27.1% acceptance rate (Metrics; Framing Requirements).
- **Open access cost**: gold OA carries an APC, amount not read; green deposit of the accepted manuscript has no embargo but stays private until publication (Open Access, Preprint Policy).
- **Sources disagree**: the two page copies differ on word limits, keyword limits and metrics (Format), so a submitter must confirm the live page.

### Best Suited For

- Conceptual or theoretical work on documents, records, classification or information practices: theory or conceptual wording appears in 45.5% of recent abstracts and the journal states a focus on theories, concepts, models, frameworks and philosophies (Methodological Preferences).
- Qualitative and library-practice studies: interviews appear in 27.8% and libraries or archives in 40.5% of recent abstracts (Orientation, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Historical and critical-review work: history wording in 15.8% and the aims text welcomes critical and scholarly reviews (Methodological Preferences, Framing Requirements).
- Sole-authored papers: 36.7% of articles in the window are single-author (Practical Concerns).

### Not Recommended For

- Experiment-led or user-study papers as the main design: experiments or user studies appear in 3.6% of recent abstracts (Methodological Preferences). The count shows the form is uncommon here, not that it is rejected.
- Authors who need a published total-time or reviewer-culture figure before choosing: none exists (Review Cycle Time, Reviewer Pool Characteristics).
- Authors who cannot anonymise their manuscript: review is double anonymous (Peer Review).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are neighbours that exist or were written in this field in this batch, listed only because they share the subject area; they are not a claim about acceptance odds. The publisher's page also lists three related Emerald journals (The Electronic Library, Online Information Review, Records Management Journal; copy dated 2026-08-15) and describes a manuscript transfer service among participating Emerald journals.
